pp:ce:2016:q1.question: Newton-Raphson method is to be used to find root of equation $3x-e^{x}+\sin x=0$. If the initial trial value for the root is taken as 0.333, the next approximation for the root would be _________

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Numerical Methods
detailed_solution.markdown:
According to Newton-Raphson Method:

$$\begin{aligned}  x_{N+1}&=X_{N}-\frac{f\left ( X_{N} \right )}{{F}'\left ( X_{N} \right )} \\    f\left ( x \right )&=3x-e^{x}+\sin x \\    {f}'\left ( x \right )&=3-e^{x}+\cos x \\ \Rightarrow  \;\;  X_{1}&=X_{0}-\frac{f\left ( 0.333 \right )}{{f}'\left ( 0.333 \right )} \\    &=0.333-\frac{3\times 0.333-e^{0.333}+\sin 0.333}{3-e^{0.333}+\cos 0.333} \\ \therefore    \;\; X_{1}&=0.36 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.36** (acceptable range: [0.355, 0.365]).

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
The PDE $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=\alpha \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}   \;\;...(i)$

Solution of (i) is,

$u\left ( x,t \right )=\left ( A\cos px+B\sin px \right )Ce^{-p^{2}\alpha t}$

Put $-p^{2}\alpha =k$

$\Rightarrow \;\;  p=\sqrt{-\frac{k}{\alpha }}=\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}i$

Putting value of p in eq.(i),

$$\begin{aligned}u\left ( x,t \right )&=\left ( A\cos \sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x+b\sin h\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x \right )Ce^{kt} \\  &=Ce^{kt}\left [ A\left \{ \frac{e^{\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}+e^{-\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}}{2} \right \}+B\left \{ \frac{e^{\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}-e^{-\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}}{2} \right \} \right ] \\  &=Ce^{kt}\left [ e^{\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}\left \{ \frac{A+B}{2} \right \}+e^{-\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}\left \{ \frac{A-B}{2} \right \} \right ] \\  &=Ce^{kt}\left [ c_{1}e^{\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}+c_{2}e^{-\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x} \right ] \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2016:q8.title: GATE CE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 8
pp:ce:2016:q8.question: The semi-compact section of a laterally unsupported steel beam has an elastic section modulus, plastic section modulus and design bending compressive stress of $500 \; cm^3, 650 \; cm^3$ and 200MPa, respectively. The design flexural capacity (expressed in kNm) of the section is ____.

detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Beams
detailed_solution.markdown:
Design flexural capacity,

$M_{d}= \beta _{b}Z_{p}\frac{f_{y}}{\gamma _{m0}}$

$\beta _{b}= 1.0$ (for plastic and compact sections)

$\; \; \; \; = \frac{Z_{e}}{Z_{p}}$ (for semi-compact sections)

$Z_{p}=\,$ Plastic section modulus

$Z_{e}=\,$ elastic section modulus

$f_{y}=\,$ yeild stress of steel provided

$\gamma_{m0}=\,$ material factor of safety of steel against yeilding

As, design bending stress is directly given,

$$\begin{aligned} M_{d}&= \beta _{b}Z_{p}f_{d} \\   &= \frac{Z_{e}}{Z_{p}}\times Z_{p}\times f_{d} \\ &= Z_{e}\times f_{d} \\   &= 500\times 10^{3}\times 200\times 10^{-6} \\  &= 100 kN-m \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **100** (acceptable range: [99.9, 100.1]).

$$\begin{aligned} \eta &=1-e^{-w\left ( A/Q \right )} \\ \eta &=\text{Collection efficiency of the precipitator} \\ w &=\text{Migration velocity,}\: cm/s \\ A &=\text{The effective collecting plate area of the precipitator,}\: m^{2} \\ Q &=\text{Gas flow through the precipitator,}\: m^{3}/s \\ 0.96&=1-e^{-\left ( \frac{w}{Q} \right )\times 5600}\; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; ...\left ( i \right ) \\ 0.97 &=1-e^{-\left ( \frac{w}{Q} \right )\times 6100}\; \; \; \; \; \; \; ...\left ( ii \right ) \end{aligned}$$

From both equations,

$\; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \frac{w}{Q}=5.748\times 10^{-4}$

Now for 99% efficiency plate area required,

$0.99=1-e^{-5.748\times 10^{-4}\times A}$

$\Rightarrow \; \; \; \; \; A=8011.78\: m^{2}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **8020** (acceptable range: [8000, 8040]).
